what: Trump Media to sell early access to key social posts

clean_source_blocks.text: Trump Media & Technology Group, which owns Truth Social, is launching a paid service to give Wall Street firms high-speed access to its most influential posts. From 1 August, instant updates will be delivered from "the highest-ranking" accounts, it said. US President Donald Trump currently has the most followers on the platform. The company behind the app hopes it will create a steady new source of money for the firm which is currently loss-making. It is likely to be aimed at financial traders who want to see market-moving news fast. Trump’s social media posts often cause sudden swings in global markets, especially when he writes about trade and tariffs. For firms, a delay of even seconds can be costly. Until now, banks and traders had to monitor the app manually. The new system will send posts directly to paying clients.
Trump Media is launching a fast, paid feed to its most influential posts for Wall Street traders.

President Trump’s social media platform announced plans Thursday to sell Wall Street firms early access to its “most market-moving” posts. Trump Media & Technology Group (TMTG), the parent company of Truth Social, said it would launch “Truth API” — a direct data feed that would give investment firms “real-time access to posts from the highest-ranking Truth Social accounts.” Trump launched Truth Social in February 2022 and has used it as his primary method of direct written communication. During his second presidential term, Trump has announced dozens of significant changes to administration policy or military operations, often swaying the stock market along the way. Application programming interfaces (APIs) are data streams commonly offered by a wide range of companies and organizations that are meant to provide immediate and secure access to information.

The BBC has contacted Trump Media for comment on whether or not the president's posts will be included in the paid feed. The White House declined to comment. While other social media networks already sell data, the move highlights the unique overlap between Trump’s private businesses and his public role as president. It would be "unprecedented" if the feature did include the president's posts, said Mark Spiegel, an investment expert from Stanphyl Capital Management. Companies that trade off the latest headlines would be "at a disadvantage" if they did not pay for quick access as they could miss out on posts that could move markets, Spiegel said. "But to put this in context, remember that Trump's posts constitute just a tiny fraction of what moves markets," he added. ---

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World | URL: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c79gw4lj89eo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss]
Trump Media & Technology Group, which owns Truth Social, is launching a paid service to give Wall Street firms high-speed access to its most influential posts.

From 1 August, instant updates will be delivered from "the highest-ranking" accounts, it said. US President Donald Trump currently has the most followers on the platform.

The company behind the app hopes it will create a steady new source of money for the firm which is currently loss-making.

It is likely to be aimed at financial traders who want to see market-moving news fast. Trump’s social media posts often cause sudden swings in global markets, especially when he writes about trade and tariffs.

For firms, a delay of even seconds can be costly. Until now, banks and traders had to monitor the app manually. The new system will send posts directly to paying clients.

"Markets already move on Truth Social posts", said Kevin McGurn, the interim boss of Trump Media, adding that the service will create a steady profit.

Trump Media did not say how much it would charge for the service.

The new commercial data feed, named Truth API, promises to deliver posts to paying institutional clients in "milliseconds".

The service will run 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

The company, which launched its social media app in 2022, said some firms have been copying its data for months without permission.

McGurn warned that Trump Media will soon block these methods, forcing firms to buy the official feed instead.

Trump could benefit substantially from the move. Since his family remains the majority shareholder in the company, the president stands to profit directly from selling expedited access to his own public statements.

The BBC has contacted Trump Media for comment on whether or not the president's posts will be included in the paid feed. The White House declined to comment.

While other social media networks already sell data, the move highlights the unique overlap between Trump’s private businesses and his public role as president.

It would be "unprecedented" if the feature did include the president's posts, said Mark Spiegel, an investment expert from Stanphyl Capital Management.

Companies that trade off the latest headlines would be "at a disadvantage" if they did not pay for quick access as they could miss out on posts that could move markets, Spiegel said.

"But to put this in context, remember that Trump's posts constitute just a tiny fraction of what moves markets," he added.

---

[Lähde: AOL | URL: https://www.aol.com/articles/wall-street-traders-soon-pay-222526000.html]
President Trump’s social media platform announced plans Thursday to sell Wall Street firms early access to its “most market-moving” posts.

Trump Media & Technology Group (TMTG), the parent company of Truth Social, said it would launch “Truth API” — a direct data feed that would give investment firms “real-time access to posts from the highest-ranking Truth Social accounts.”

Trump launched Truth Social in February 2022 and has used it as his primary method of direct written communication. During his second presidential term, Trump has announced dozens of significant changes to administration policy or military operations, often swaying the stock market along the way.

Application programming interfaces (APIs) are data streams commonly offered by a wide range of companies and organizations that are meant to provide immediate and secure access to information.

Both amateur and professional investors use APIs of key financial or economic data, including one offered by the Labor Department, to craft their trades.

Truth API, which TMTG aims to launch Aug. 1, would give the nation’s top investment firms the earliest access to market-moving posts on Truth Social, allowing algorithmic trading programs to act even quicker on the news.

“Markets already move on Truth Social posts,” said TMTG interim CEO Kevin McGurn. “Truth API delivers a direct, licensed, real-time feed of the platform’s most market-moving Truths while advancing our strategy to monetize proprietary assets through a high-margin, recurring revenue stream.

“As adoption grows, we expect Truth API to become a meaningful, ongoing source of revenue for the company, creating lasting value for shareholders,” he continued.

Truth API could create another venue through which Trump could personally profit through a connection to his presidency.

Trump indirectly owns roughly 53 percent of TMTG through shares he transferred to a trust in December 2024, one month before he took office, amid growing concerns about potential conflicts of interest.

Earlier this month, the president disclosed making more than $2 billion in income during his first year back in office, including more than $1 billion in income linked to World Liberty Financial, his family’s cryptocurrency company.

Despite his skepticism of the technology during his first presidential term, Trump embraced cryptocurrency ahead of his 2024 presidential campaign. Soon after, his family crypto company launched several products, including a stablecoin.

payload.title: Trump Media alkaa myydä Wall Streetille nopeaa pääsyä Truth Social -julkaisuihin
payload.summary: Truth API välittää vaikutusvaltaisten Truth Social -tilien julkaisuja reaaliaikaisesti maksaville sijoitusyhtiöille. Donald Trumpin omien julkaisujen kuulumista palveluun ei ole vahvistettu.
payload.content:
Truth Socialin omistava Trump Media & Technology Group alkaa 1. elokuuta tarjota Wall Streetin sijoitusyhtiöille maksullista Truth API -tietosyötettä, joka välittää vaikutusvaltaisimpien Truth Social -tilien julkaisut suoraan asiakkaiden järjestelmiin. Palvelu lupaa reaaliaikaisen pääsyn markkinoita mahdollisesti liikuttaviin viesteihin tilanteessa, jossa jo muutaman sekunnin viive voi olla kaupankävijälle kallis.

## Rajapinta korvaa käsiseurannan

Yhtiön mukaan syöte kattaa palvelun ”korkeimmalle luokiteltujen” tilien julkaisuja. Maksavat asiakkaat saisivat päivitykset heti sen sijaan, että pankkien ja muiden markkinatoimijoiden pitäisi seurata Truth Socialia käsin. Rajapinta eli API on tietovirta, jonka avulla tiedot voidaan toimittaa nopeasti ja suojatusti suoraan niitä käyttäville organisaatioille. Tällaiset rajapinnat ovat yleisiä, ja muutkin sosiaalisen median yhtiöt myyvät dataa.

Donald Trumpilla on Truth Socialissa enemmän seuraajia kuin kenelläkään muulla palvelun käyttäjällä. Hän käynnisti alustan helmikuussa 2022 ja on käyttänyt sitä ensisijaisena suoran kirjallisen viestinnän kanavanaan. Toisella presidenttikaudellaan Trump on ilmoittanut siellä kymmenistä merkittävistä hallintopolitiikan tai sotilasoperaatioiden muutoksista, ja hänen viestinsä ovat heiluttaneet osakemarkkinoita. Erityisesti kauppaa ja tulleja koskevat julkaisut ovat aiheuttaneet nopeita liikkeitä maailmanmarkkinoilla.

Trump Media hakee uudesta palvelusta tasaista tulonlähdettä, sillä yhtiö on tällä hetkellä tappiollinen. Maksullinen suora syöte kohdistuu toimijoille, joille markkinoita liikuttavan tiedon nopea saaminen on arvokasta. Aiemmin niiden on täytynyt seurata sovellusta itse, mutta Truth API lähettää valitut julkaisut suoraan maksaville asiakkaille.

## Trumpin omien julkaisujen asema on avoin

Avoinna on kuitenkin keskeinen kysymys: kuuluvatko presidentti Trumpin omat julkaisut maksulliseen syötteeseen. Trump Medialta pyydettiin asiasta kommenttia, mutta vastausta ei ollut uutisen julkaisuhetkellä saatavilla. Valkoinen talo kieltäytyi kommentoimasta. Epäselvyys korostaa Trumpin yksityisen liiketoiminnan ja hänen julkisen presidentinroolinsa poikkeuksellista päällekkäisyyttä.

Stanphyl Capital Managementin sijoitusasiantuntija Mark Spiegel arvioi, että presidentin julkaisujen sisällyttäminen palveluun olisi ennennäkemätöntä. Hänen mukaansa tuoreimpien otsikoiden perusteella kauppaa käyvät yhtiöt voisivat joutua epäedulliseen asemaan, jos ne eivät maksaisi nopeasta pääsystä ja jäisivät ilman markkinoita liikuttavaa viestiä. Spiegel kuitenkin muistutti, että Trumpin julkaisut ovat vain pieni osa kaikesta markkinoihin vaikuttavasta tiedosta.
summary_bullets: Truth API käynnistyy 1. elokuuta ja välittää valittujen Truth Social -tilien julkaisuja reaaliaikaisesti.
Palvelu on suunnattu sijoitusyhtiöille, joille muutaman sekunnin viive voi olla kaupankäynnissä kallis.
Donald Trumpin omien julkaisujen kuulumista maksulliseen syötteeseen ei ole vahvistettu.
payload.journalist_note: Donald Trumpin julkaisujen kuuluminen maksulliseen tietosyötteeseen on vahvistamatta, ja epävarmuus on ilmaistu tekstissä.

During his second presidential term, Trump has announced dozens of significant changes to administration policy or military operations, often swaying the stock market along the way. Application programming interfaces (APIs) are data streams commonly offered by a wide range of companies and organizations that are meant to provide immediate and secure access to information.

The BBC has contacted Trump Media for comment on whether or not the president's posts will be included in the paid feed. The White House declined to comment. While other social media networks already sell data, the move highlights the unique overlap between Trump’s private businesses and his public role as president. It would be "unprecedented" if the feature did include the president's posts, said Mark Spiegel, an investment expert from Stanphyl Capital Management. Companies that trade off the latest headlines would be "at a disadvantage" if they did not pay for quick access as they could miss out on posts that could move markets, Spiegel said. "But to put this in context, remember that Trump's posts constitute just a tiny fraction of what moves markets," he added. ---
